newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH SAK SETS TARGETS FOR DECIDING EMU STANCE.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH SAK SETS TARGETS FOR DECIDING EMU STANCE.

text.p: Finland's biggest trade union group on Friday unveiled some targets, which if implemented could lead it to adopt a favourable stance to Finland joining the planned third phase of Europe's Economic and Monetary Union.
Lauri Ihalainen, chairman of the Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK), told its council's autumn meeting the SAK would decide its EMU stance next autumn.
Repeating an earlier SAK council resolution, Ihalainen said Finnish EMU membership was not possible unless employment improved substantially.

He called for negotiations between central trade unions and employer confederations, and listed three issues of key importance for the SAK -- a 1.1-million mainly blue-collar central union grouping most employees in big export sectors.
"SAK proposes that the labour market organisations would next spring negotiate a joint agreement on some EMU issues concerning labour market policies," Ihalainen told the council.
The agreement should state that in EMU, nobody will try to gain a competitive advantage by dumping wages and that the Finnish collective wage bargaining system will remain in place, he said.
"The labour market parties must unequivocally be able to say that ... nominal wages will not have to be lowered or other terms of employment weakened due to (Finnish) EMU membership," Ihalainen said.
He also called for tripartite talks between unions, employers and the government about national buffer funds aimed at cushioning the impact of cyclical downturns.

But Ihalainen said the already existing funds, like work pension funds and other funding systems, could form the starting point of these talks. Finnish employer groups have repeatedly opposed the creation of new buffer funds.
